opportunities.title: Three of six lodestar_epochs fields do not match the subgraph, and the parity script never compared any of them
opportunities.summary: Measured while implementing the epoch comparison for #1076 (PR #1111). The parity script had `EPOCH_N` computed, exported and never compared, printing `count-only: mutable aggregates have no historical snapshot surface` instead. Two claims in that line are wrong, and the second is the interesting one. **There is an as-of surface.** `lodestar_epochs` aggregates with no block filter, but every epoch except the newest is immutable at a pin: rewards are grouped by the event's own `currentEpoch`, which is monotonic in block, and fees/signal are bucketed by `block_number BETWEEN start_block AND end_block`, a window that closes once the successor epoch is first observed. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50

opportunities.title: [Bounty $1500] logaddexp / logaddexp2: overflow-safe reformulation
opportunities.summary: ## Summary `ttnn.logaddexp` and `ttnn.logaddexp2` are composed as `log(exp(a) + exp(b))` literally, so they return `±inf` for arguments whose exact result is an ordinary finite number. The whole point of a log-sum-exp primitive is that it does not overflow; this one overflows at `|a| > 88.7`, which is inside the normal working range of any log-domain computation. Both directions fail: `logaddexp(100, 0)` returns `inf` where the exact answer is `100`, and `logaddexp(-100, -100)` returns `-inf` where the exact answer is `-99.31`. There is no representable-range argument available here, because the result is boxed in by its own inputs: ``` max(a, b) <= logaddexp(a, b) <= max(a, b) + ln 2 ``` If both arguments are finite the answer is finite and within 0.694 of one of them, so an `inf` return is never a range limitation — it is always the intermediate. ## Current state measured on ttsim ttsim 1.9.7, `Arch.BLACKHOLE`, `ttnn.logaddexp` called directly: | a | b | chip | exact | | |---|---|---|---|---| | 100 | 0 | `inf` | 100.000000 | ✗ | | 89 | 0 | `inf` | 89.000000 | ✗ | | 90 | 89 | `inf` | 90.313263 | ✗ | | 100 | 100 | `inf` | 100.693146 | ✗ | | 200 | 199 | `inf` | 200.313263 | ✗ | | −1
